headline: Mariana has lost 8% of her body weight (77.9 to 71.7 kg) from Sep 5 to Nov 24, 2026, and her son and primary caregiver reports exhaustion and has asked for respite; a Nov 26 chart correction disputes the weight-loss note.

items.statement: Weight fell steadily from 77.9 kg (Sep 5) to 75.7 kg (Oct 1), 73.6 kg (Oct 28) and 71.7 kg (Nov 24), a loss of 6.2 kg (8.0%). On Nov 24 the dietitian documented poor appetite, skipped breakfast and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan was an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: The weights, dates, 6.2 kg (8.0%) loss, and the Nov 24 dietitian findings and plan all match the vitals record and note n002.

items.statement: On Sep 27 the social worker met with Marcus, her son and primary caregiver. He reported exhaustion, poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: Note n001 matches every detail: Sep 27 social worker meeting, Marcus as son and primary caregiver, exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: A Nov 26 chart correction, attributed to Dr. Nakamura, says the Nov 24 weight-loss entry was documented on the wrong participant and should be disregarded. The structured weight record independently shows the 4 readings and the 8% decline for Mariana. The original event is reported as documented, and the conflict needs resolving.
items.verifier_note: Note n013 is a Nov 26 correction attributed to Dr. Nakamura saying the Nov 24 weight-loss entry was on the wrong participant. The vitals record shows 4 readings and an 8% decline. The statement reports the original event as documented and flags the conflict for the team to resolve, as it should.

questions_for_team: Which record is correct: the Nov 26 correction saying the Nov 24 weight note belongs to another participant, or the vitals record showing a steady decline for Mariana? Can the weights be verified and the correction source confirmed?
Should the dietitian's plan (supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check) go ahead while the conflict is resolved?
What respite and evening support can be arranged for Marcus, and has anything been put in place since Sep 27?
Are the PCP notes of Sep 2, Sep 27 and Nov 27 (chronic conditions stable) aware of the weight trend?

args.query: fall, dizziness, near-fall, injury, back or hip pain
lab results eGFR creatinine hemoglobin B12 injection cholesterol
ADL cognition mood depression day center attendance missed

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and discharge summaries.

Falls and near-falls: count and document any falls, injuries, or fall-risk screen changes. Note osteoporosis (2015) raises fracture stakes, so flag any fall with possible fracture or new back/hip pain.
Chest pain and cardiac events (ischemic heart disease): review any chest pain reports, nitroglycerin spray use or refills, ED visits for cardiac symptoms, and any new cardiology referrals or testing.

Blood pressure trend: review all recorded readings in the window against prior baseline, note any hypotension symptoms (dizziness, orthostatic change), and check whether readings are documented on metoprolol.
Heart rate trend on metoprolol succinate: review pulse readings for bradycardia or symptoms such as fatigue or lightheadedness.

Glycemic control (type 2 diabetes, prediabetes history, hyperglycemia): review HbA1c, fasting glucose, and any glucose readings in the window; check for hypoglycemia events. Note that no diabetes-specific glucose-lowering medication appears on the active list. Confirm whether this reflects a deliberate plan, a documentation gap, or a med list update, and let the prescriber decide.
Kidney function (CKD stage 1 due to diabetes): review most recent eGFR, creatinine, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and any new labs ordered or overdue in the window.

Lipids and statin therapy: review triglyceride and LDL results and confirm simvastatin status. Note that simvastatin 20 mg is the only lipid-lowering agent listed despite ischemic heart disease and hypertriglyceridemia; flag for prescriber review rather than recommending a change.
Anemia and B12: review hemoglobin/CBC trends and confirm vitamin B12 injection schedule is current, with any missed or delayed doses documented.

Medication changes since last review: list all starts, stops, dose changes, and refill gaps for the four active medications and any new prescriptions from outside providers; reconcile against pharmacy fill history. Confirm no allergies are recorded and verify that allergy status is accurate.
Weight and BMI trend (BMI 30+, metabolic syndrome): review weight measurements across the window and compare with prior baseline; note any unintentional change.
Function, ADLs, and cognition: update ADL/IADL status, mobility, and any cognitive screening results; note any decline reported by participant, caregiver, or staff.

Mood, social engagement, and PACE attendance: review center attendance and missed days, mood screen results, and any behavioral or social concerns; check caregiver situation and any caregiver strain or changes in living arrangements.

Care-plan items due: list any assessments, reviews, labs, eye/foot exams, bone density follow-up, or preventive items that are due or overdue by the 2026-11-30 review date, and flag items for the IDT agenda.

Summarize for the IDT: what changed since last review, open questions for clinicians (glycemic regimen, lipid therapy, BP/HR response to metoprolol, kidney monitoring), and items needing decisions by the prescriber or team. Do not make treatment recommendations.
